Double machine learning of the effect of alert complexity

Source: R/cxvol.R
cxdml.Rd

The interactive regression model of Chernozhukov et al. (2018) for the effect of complex alert profiles (cx) on placement volatility (vm) on the person-year table, by dmlx(): random forests (or another learner of dmlx()) for the outcome regressions and the propensity, nfold-fold cross-fitting, propensities kept within trim of 0 and 1, covariates gender, age group, regional cluster and (pooled, with yterm) fiscal year. Both the average effect (ATE) and the effect on the treated (ATTE) are given, from one set of cross-fitted nuisances. The same refusals as cxvol() apply.

Usage

cxdml(
  x,
  by = c("pool", "year"),
  yterm = TRUE,
  lrn = "forest",
  ntree = 500,
  nfold = 3,
  trim = 0.01,
  seed = 1,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A person-year table from otpyr(), or what otpyr() takes (a data frame of the release or a table key).

by

"pool" for the years together, "year" for each year.

yterm

TRUE to adjust for the fiscal year in the pooled propensity and count models.

lrn

The learner of dmlx(), for both nuisances.

ntree

The trees of a forest.

nfold

The folds of the cross-fitting: a whole number from 2.

trim

Propensities are kept within trim of 0 and 1.

seed

The seed of the folds and of the learners.

...

Passed to otpyr() when x is not a person-year table.

Value

An object of class cxdml: a data frame with one row per sample and estimand (sample, n, estimand, est, se, lo, hi).

References

Chernozhukov, V., Chetverikov, D., Demirer, M., Duflo, E., Hansen, C., Newey, W. and Robins, J. (2018). Double/debiased machine learning for treatment and structural parameters. The Econometrics Journal, 21(1), C1-C68. doi:10.1111/ectj.12097

Examples

set.seed(5)
n <- 400
p <- data.frame(year = sample(2025:2026, n, TRUE),
                gender = sample(c("Male", "Female"), n, TRUE),
                age = sample(c("18 to 24", "25 to 49"), n, TRUE),
                rc = sample(c("A", "B"), n, TRUE), cx = rbinom(n, 1, 0.3))
p$vm <- rpois(n, exp(-1.5 + 0.4 * p$cx))
cxdml(p, lrn = "glm")
#> cxdml: interactive model, effect of cx on vm (additive scale)
#>     sample   n estimand    est      se      lo     hi
#>  2025-2026 400      ATE 0.1571 0.06122 0.03713 0.2771
#>  2025-2026 400     ATTE 0.1336 0.05927 0.01742 0.2498
